Part of Just Every · MIT licensed

Watch the full demo · 56 seconds


Your agent's fix, your reply and the customer's thanks, in one conversation.


Move in from Zendesk: imports keep source details and never message your customers.

# HappyToHelp HappyToHelp is an open-source support workspace with a customer chat widget, shared inbox, AI-assisted replies, help centers, customer context and optional work delegated to your own Codex or Claude. It works with human replies without an AI provider. The editable React application runs on Cloudflare Workers with Hono, D1, R2, Queues and Durable Objects. ## Release 0.4.25 Deploy version 0.4.25, tagged **`v0.4.25`** once published. v0.4.24 is the upgrade baseline; upgrades are qualified from v0.4.24, v0.4.23 and v0.4.22. The pinned installer remains rer 0.2.112. - **Managed installation verification:** includes the generator-recorded portable contract anchor. A managed source copy with only its own two installation commits can now run the existing contract check without the publisher's Git history. Setup, build, verification and artifact creation keep their declared checks; this fixes the `contract_anchor_missing` failure after copying v0.4.24. - **Unused legacy reservations and attachment custody:** the original installation owner can approve a different package fingerprint after an unused adoption reservation expires, is discarded or pauses with an error, provided no destination workspace was created and no erasure or deletion fence applies. Created provenance remains permanent, and the old fingerprint stays closed. Canonical attachment custody transfers with the unused reservation, including already cleaned coordinates; old cleanup jobs cannot delete a replacement package's live attachments or stop its import wakeups. A cleanup already deleting objects must finish its claim before that handoff. - **Clearer imported history and results:** historical staff display as Former staff, while historical contact, AI and system authors retain their distinctions; none gains native membership or assignment authority. Move in shows the actual pause code and a matching explanation, distinguishes historical verification from current source availability, and labels historical memberships as granting no access. Reconciliation tables can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard, including on phones. Imported AI profiles remain disabled and imported workflows stay draft. - **Tickets and mailbox setup:** a ticket starting with an internal note can be created before a mailbox is connected, without sending email. Email-first tickets still require a connected mailbox. Email settings explain missing installation prerequisites and local-trial limits, with hosted Google, Microsoft, IMAP/SMTP and forwarding instructions. A local trial sends and receives no email; use website chat to try conversations. Connecting a mailbox does not configure sign-in or invitation mail. Live mailbox/provider qualification remains separate. - **Fresh hosted installs:** native setup, ordinary support and the ticket/mailbox guidance above are active. The importer runner and adoption remain inert until a legacy package is imported through the approved flow; cleanup continues for already registered packages. Updating alone starts no import, sends no mail and grants no historical-user access. The corrected mail declaration and rer 0.2.112 are retained. Real-customer remote importer use, signed migration-before-Worker delivery and live-provider qualification remain separate; this preparation authorizes no production import or cutover. - **Migrations:** no migrations since v0.4.24. The inventory remains 195 files, byte-identical to v0.4.24, so its applied migration ledger stays unchanged. A v0.4.23 installation applies 328, 329, 331 and 332 once in filename order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327, retaining the published buyer steps. There is no migration 326 or 330. Update from v0.4.24 without resetting; v0.4.23 and v0.4.22 are also upgrade baselines. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. A v0.4.24 installation applies no migration. Stop the old Worker before applying any missing migrations on older installations: v0.4.23 applies 328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql, 329_legacy_package_custody.sql, 331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql and 332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql once in that order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic; v0.4.22 first applies 327_legacy_import_worker.sql. Retain those releases' published buyer steps, including 332's conditional cleanup of only an untouched empty inventory marker. Earlier installations first apply every other missing published migration in filename order. There is no migration 326 or 330 in this release. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. V1 source stays cleanup-only and must never be relabeled v2; incomplete cleanup remains pending. No reset, mail activation, recovery adoption, production import, cutover or production deployment is part of this preparation. See [RELEASE.json](RELEASE.json), [Updates and recovery](docs/INDEPENDENT-RELEASE.md) and [the changelog](CHANGELOG.md). Version 0.4.0 adds Move in for reviewed support-history imports, resolution feedback with workspace-calendar Reports, Connections with scoped API tokens, signed webhook events and Slack delivery, and the `rer` local path. Native passwords, owners and data are kept. Before the updated Worker serves traffic, back up and apply the ten additive migrations `0110_move_in.sql` to `119_local_portability.sql` in order; an existing 0.3 installation follows [Upgrading from 0.3.x](OPERATIONS.md#upgrading-from-03x). [The changelog](CHANGELOG.md) lists every change. Known limits: - Accessibility is on a confirmed owner **HOLD**; no WCAG conformance is claimed. - `rer export` archives cover D1, R2 and **Durable Object** storage (with a digest); full Base-data equivalence is not yet established. - Hosted operating costs are **unmeasured**; timed activation and paid-provider execution are not qualified. - Imports and connections are qualified with **synthetic fixtures** only, without real vendor exports or live Slack. - No hosted installation, compliance or FedRAMP qualification is claimed. - The hosted service at **app.happytohelp.com** is separate legacy production and is not part of this release. ## Run it on your computer The [install and run guide](docs/INSTALLER.md) covers installation, local sign-in and stopping the app, step by step. The [Run HappyToHelp page](https://happytohelp.com/run) has the quick-start command. Start it with one line. You need **Node.js 22 or later** (with npm) and Git; check with `node --version`. ```sh npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-happytohelp ``` That clones HappyToHelp into `run-happytohelp`, provisions the checkout's own pinned Node and pnpm, installs dependencies, sets up a local owner and starts the app. To set it up without starting it, use `npx -y @runeditrun/rer setup just-every/run-happytohelp`. Without Node, `curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh -s -- dev just-every/run-happytohelp` brings its own. To start it again later, run `cd run-happytohelp && rer dev`. The install also downloads Chromium (about 280 MB, into your user cache) the first time: `rer verify` and the browser checks run in it. Dev uses its local address for the chat widget and generates a private owner password. Wait for `RER_READY`, then open the `RER_OPEN` address to enter as the real local owner and reach **Setup**. No private answers, email service or AI account are needed. Use `rer dev --stop` from the checkout to stop the managed app. Already running 0.3? Keep your checkout and data, and follow [Upgrading from 0.3.x](OPERATIONS.md#upgrading-from-03x) instead. See [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md) for private setup answers and [Local command reference](RUN-LOCALLY.md) for ports, preview and idle shutdown. To try the customer flow, [install the widget on a local page](docs/INSTALLER.md#try-the-customer-widget-locally), send a visitor message and reply from **Inbox**. Set that page's exact origin in **Settings → Widget → Settings**; the app's own origin remains allowed. A visitor's entered email can receive operator replies even when their identity is labelled **Unverified**. Local visitor and teammate mail is suppressed without storage or external sending. With a hosted sender, **Email sent to provider · delivery not confirmed** on a reply means acceptance, not confirmed inbox delivery. ## Choose how to run it Local dev is a loopback trial on your computer. An online installation in your own Cloudflare account lets the widget on your website reach the workspace. Both use the same rer commands. An independently managed project may select its own operating contract; this seed's CLI is not a platform admission requirement. ## Deploy to your own Cloudflare account For a new installation, acquire **`v0.4.25` once published**, after installing `rer` as shown above: ```sh git clone --branch v0.4.25 https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp cd run-happytohelp ``` Start with a local build and validation: ```sh rer deploy --dry-run ``` This needs no provider credentials, makes no Cloudflare requests, sends no mail and changes nothing remotely. It validates the deployment declaration and builds the application locally. The completion report lists any inputs needed for a real deploy; remote resources, credential validity, target secrets and remote readiness remain unchecked. For a real deployment, read [deployment prerequisites](OPERATIONS.md#deploy-to-your-cloudflare-account). When rer says **See the deploy-kit owner-account instructions**, it means [What you need first](OPERATIONS.md#what-you-need-first): how to make the Cloudflare API token and find the account ID. Configure the real declaration and private account credentials, then: ```sh rer deploy --environment production ``` The contract also requires a separately started **read-only provider preflight** with explicit owner consent and the owner's scoped Cloudflare token. For an existing Worker, that preflight permits only the account's Workers subdomain and the Worker's settings and secret names (three GETs), with no mail or mutations. That separate preflight is not yet implemented or live-qualified; the local dry run does not perform it or prove remote readiness. For a new installation with outbound email, also supply real `EMAIL_PROVIDER`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY` and `OWNER_EMAIL` inputs in an owned 0600 `--env-file`; the owner email must receive sign-in mail. Existing installations retain held secrets. The seven optional mailbox settings can stay unset. Remote provisioning remains separately unqualified. ```sh rer deploy --environment production --env-file ~/happytohelp-production.env ``` Deployment provisions declared resources, applies migrations, publishes and checks health through Base deploy-kit. After a healthy deploy, `rer deploy` claims the owner named by `OWNER_EMAIL` (a real setup owner, or the value you supply privately) with a one-time token it then removes. Open your Worker's address and sign in by email as that owner to reach **Setup**. The owner's name is derived from their email. A Workers hostname does not name your business: a `workers.dev` website defaults to **My workspace** regardless of owner email. An explicitly chosen native workspace name takes precedence; you can change it in Project settings. Deploy refuses the local placeholder `owner@run-happytohelp.test`: it has no mailbox. For a real deployment, supply `OWNER_EMAIL` privately in your environment or an owned 0600 `--env-file`. The local dry run can list missing production inputs without requiring them. `rer signin --environment production` directs you to this installation's `/login` page. HappyToHelp uses its native email/password sign-in; the command cannot mint an owner link. If mail fails, follow the working mail recovery in [operations](OPERATIONS.md#claim-your-new-installation). `rer deploy --environment NAME --remove --yes` removes that environment's created Worker, D1, R2 and queues in one pass, including uploaded attachments in its R2 bucket, and reads back that each is gone. Export anything you need before removal. Hosted installation and real provider execution are not qualified by this release. ## What you need and what it costs HappyToHelp is MIT licensed with no seats or subscription fees. Your Cloudflare, email and optional AI providers bill your own accounts. Enable R2 and the account capabilities required by the declaration before deployment. An email sender must be verified. Local development needs no external mail or AI credential. Configure optional model keys, the Apify crawler (for website sources larger than the built-in reader's 40 pages; see [Website knowledge](docs/website-knowledge.md)), Qdrant search, GitHub and email only when you need them. See [Optional features and their settings](OPERATIONS.md#optional-features-and-their-settings) and [Measure local usage and costs](OPERATIONS.md#measure-local-usage-and-costs). The optional [local agent](local-agent/README.md) runs on the computer doing the support work and has its own runtime prerequisites. ## After you install Your workspace is already set up when you first sign in. It has a starter assistant for visitors, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds an `INBOUND_EMAIL_TOKEN`, and mail that leaves from the installation's own sender until your sending domain is verified. The inbound token authenticates incoming mail; configure your email provider's domain routing and webhook before replies can arrive. Creating the workspace may send you one welcome email. Use **Setup**, the first entry in **Settings** (its row there counts what still needs you; an empty inbox links to it): **Needs you** lists what cannot be done for you (the widget on your website, an AI key and, with a hosted email provider, your sending domain's DNS records), and **What we've set** lists the rest. Anything under **Needs you** can be skipped for now and picked up later from **Skipped**. The system runs its own checks while Setup is open, and what it confirms is counted ("N of M confirmed", without what you skipped): mail to you, sender DNS, inbound mail, model access, spend ceilings, widget origin and an authenticated widget visit. Saved settings alone do not complete them. Add the widget through **Settings → Widget**, set its exact [website origin](docs/SETUP-WORKFLOW.md#the-widget-website-origin), publish useful articles and invite teammates through **Settings → Agents**. By default the widget does not ask for an email. For visitors to receive replies by email, enable **Settings → Widget → Settings → Required contact details → Require email**. The visitor enters their address before sending a message; operator replies can then use it on a hosted installation with email sending configured. ## Set up AI replies Your starter assistant answers visitors by itself, from the help articles you publish and from what we read on your website, and within your daily limits, as soon as the installation has a key from an AI provider. Until then, new conversations stay with your team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. 1. **Get an API key** from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI or OpenRouter. The provider bills you for what you use. 2. **Add the key to your installation** under the name for that provider: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (or `GEMINI_API_KEY`), `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. The setup answers can store one at install time (see [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md#private-setup-answers)). - **On Cloudflare:** in the Cloudflare dashboard, open your Worker, go to **Settings → Variables and Secrets** and add the key as a secret. You can also set it in your terminal before you run `rer deploy --environment production` (see [Optional features and their settings](OPERATIONS.md#optional-features-and-their-settings)). - **On your own computer:** add a line such as `OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key` to a file named `.dev.vars` in the `run-happytohelp` folder, then restart the app. 3. **Setup notices the key.** While the starter assistant is untouched it uses a model of whichever provider's key is installed, and Setup confirms the key with the provider. To use a different assistant, open **Settings → AI**, add one (or choose **Customize** on an existing one), enter the **Model** it uses and keep it **Enabled**. Then, under **Responder defaults**, choose which assistant answers visitors, and with **AI replies** whether its replies are sent automatically, kept as drafts for your team to send, or turned off. In draft, a reply your local computer agent prepares waits in its report for you to use and send, and a visitor who writes while your team is away gets your away message, as if no assistant were assigned. Such a visitor's conversation also appears in **Open** and **Unassigned**. Keep key values out of chat messages and the browser. To cap what visitors can spend, see [Limits and AI ceilings](docs/PUBLIC-LIMITS.md). ## Try a demo inbox When your workspace has no conversations yet, the inbox greets you with one next action and a quiet **Try a demo inbox** link under it. The link creates a separate, clearly labelled workspace called **Demo inbox · Northstar Outfitters**, with: - fictional customer conversations - a drafting assistant you can edit - three published FAQ articles Creating the demo makes no AI, email or other provider calls. To see AI drafting, open a demo conversation and press **Generate**. HappyToHelp then drafts suggested replies for you to review, using your AI provider. The demo's assistant uses OpenAI's `gpt-5.6-luna` model, so this needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` unless you change the assistant's model (see [Set up AI replies](#set-up-ai-replies)). Generate never sends a reply to a customer. When you are done, delete the demo workspace from its settings. ## Support history, feedback, Reports and connections Owner/admin **Move in** reviews five kinds: conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Inspect per-kind plans, rejections, omissions, conflicts and publication changes; approve, resume a stopped batch, follow report links, repeat or undo through the same current role checks. Original source IDs, timestamps and private notes remain attributed; published articles stay published and drafts stay drafts. Apply and undo are inert: no mail, widget messages, model work, assignment or connection notifications. [The moving-in guide](docs/moving-in.md) explains formats, source custody and conflict-safe undo. Validation is **documented-format, synthetic-only; realExport: not-supplied**. The 9 October owner ruling requires exact business-state equality on repeat and undo. Platform counters/sequences, audit and import journals are excluded; business notes, source links, identities and native contact content remain checked. A resolved widget conversation asks **Did this answer your question?** with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Only its owning visitor session can rate its current closed cycle; widget action limits apply and changes retain history. Native records store AI, assisted, human or unknown provenance. A visitor message reopens the conversation; another resolution gets its own record. Reports uses the workspace timezone and 7/30/90-day or custom calendar ranges for volume, median/p90 first response and resolution times, AI resolution and satisfaction counts/rates, daily series and latest comments with conversation links. Conversation and summary CSV exports guard formula-leading cells. Imports are excluded and Reports calls no model. [The Reports guide](docs/reports.md) and [workspace workflows](docs/WORKSPACE-WORKFLOWS.md) explain the denominators. Settings offers seven explicit token scopes, optional expiry, one-time secret display, hashed storage, revoke, last use and audit. [The API guide](docs/api.md) contains thirteen Bearer-only operations. Webhooks support four signed events, explicit test sends and safe attempt logs; public HTTPS destinations are checked against SSRF. Slack has incoming-webhook and bot-plus-channel modes. Both have recorded-response checks only; **live Slack: not-supplied**. Deliveries use ordinary platform HTTPS fetch with manual redirects. Every 3xx fails without following its Location. Requests are limited to 1 MiB, responses (including streams) to 64 KiB, and the entire request/response to 10 seconds. Public HTTPS destination syntax and literal IP validation remain enforced; this edition does not claim DNS pinning. Base HTTP 500 remains uncertain without automatic replay; 429 retains four bounded attempts with the same logical identity and exact body. Installed owners land on the Setup page, where the system has already done what it can and lists only what needs them; new workspaces lead with the widget snippet, with secrets and verification controls under **Advanced**. Empty inboxes offer widget installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow the selected workspace; visitors intentionally see the operator's display name. Local development suppresses email without storing messages. ## Export conversations In **Reports**, choose **Export workspace conversations (JSON)**. The `transcripts.json` download includes every workspace conversation across all dates and imports, with its messages, private notes and attachment names and metadata. Attachment bytes remain in the workspace; use the portable backup for those. Exports ask for recent confirmation: accounts without a second factor can choose **Email me a sign-in link**, press **Sign in** from their mailbox in the same browser, then return and press **Continue**. This also works for older email-claimed owners whose generated password was never known. After mailbox confirmation, **Profile → Security** lets you set a new password without the old one. Enrolled second factors remain required. Reports and its analytics CSVs exclude empty widget conversations. ## Contributor setup For work on the source, select Node **22.20.0** and pnpm **10.12.4**: ```sh pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm exec rer describe --json pnpm exec rer check --profile first-party ``` ## Verify ```sh rer verify ``` The complete target checks the contract, real build, typecheck, native runtime, command journey, current workflows and selected Base copies. For a change, run its touched tests plus `pnpm run typecheck`; CI is the full wall. Browser suites and full verification run on the designated remote runner. Provider fixtures prove local protocol behavior; hosted acceptance and paid-provider execution require separate evidence. Preserve [the current holds](HANDOVER.md#acceptance-boundaries). ## Where to go next Development lives in [just-every/run-happytohelp](https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp); the private repository is retained for research and evidence only. - [Install](docs/INSTALLER.md): private answers and the rer journey. - [First-run setup](docs/SETUP-WORKFLOW.md): one-screen first run and the Setup page. - [Operations](OPERATIONS.md): configuration, data movement, deployment and recovery. - [Updates and recovery](docs/INDEPENDENT-RELEASE.md): owner customizations and backups. - [Product contract](CONTRACT.md) and [acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md): requirements and proof. - [Authoring](docs/AUTHORING.md): source selection and exact Base copies. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party asset notices remain under [docs/licenses](docs/licenses).
